    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca7-25-02876 / USCOURTS-ca7-25-02876-0

    FAPD-AI: In a nonprecedential order, the Seventh Circuit affirmed the Central District of Illinois's denial of a third motion for compassionate release under 18 U.S.C. § 3582(c)(1)(A)(i) filed by Timothy B. Fredrickson, a federal prisoner serving 200 months for sexual exploitation of a minor. The court found no abuse of discretion, holding that a single latent tuberculosis diagnosis and general measles statistics did not establish an ongoing outbreak, imminent risk of one, or an ongoing public health emergency at FCI Seagoville under U.S.S.G. § 1B1.13(b)(1)(D). The court further noted that, because no extraordinary and compelling reason was shown, the district court was not required to consider the § 3553(a) factors, citing Rutherford v. United States.     Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca6-25-04026 / USCOURTS-ca6-25-04026-0

    FAPD-AI: In an opinion not recommended for publication filed November 18, 2026, the Sixth Circuit affirmed the Northern District of Ohio's grant of summary judgment to Tenisha Wilson and Denman Gordon on their claim that the City of South Euclid, Ohio abandoned its interest in a strip of 'Laurens Avenue,' a platted but unbuilt street abutting Wilson's property, which reverted to the abutting owners.     Congressional Record · govinfo API · CREC-2026-11-18 / CREC-2026-11-18-pt1-PgH6262-5

    FAPD-AI: Representative Mast moved to suspend the rules and pass H.R. 5490, the "Dismantle Foreign Scam Syndicates Act," as amended, and the bill text is reproduced. The bill's findings describe "pig butchering" investment scams and scam compounds in Burma, Laos, and Cambodia, and it directs the President to establish within 30 days an interagency Task Force chaired by the Secretary of State to develop a comprehensive U.S. Government strategy within 240 days and to submit annual reports for five years. The Task Force would terminate five years after enactment, and the text provided is truncated before its final provisions. CREC-SEL-01

    Preventive Health Savings Act (opens in a new tab)
    Congressional Record · govinfo API · CREC-2026-11-18 / CREC-2026-11-18-pt1-PgH6266

    FAPD-AI: H.R. 4464, the "Preventive Health Savings Act," would add a new subsection (h) to section 202 of the Congressional Budget and Impoundment Control Act of 1974. Upon request by the designated congressional leaders, the CBO Director would determine whether proposed legislation yields net reductions in budget outlays in budgetary outyears through preventive health care, defined as two consecutive 10-year periods beginning 10 years after the current fiscal year, and any such estimate would be supplementary and not used for budgetary enforcement controls. During floor debate under suspension, Representatives Arrington and Boyle described the bill as allowing analysis beyond the standard 10-year scoring window for health-related savings. CREC-SEL-01

  • Observed at 09:02:26 Eastern time ET
    Settlement Agreement Information Database Act of 2026 (opens in a new tab)
    Congressional Record · govinfo API · CREC-2026-11-18 / CREC-2026-11-18-pt1-PgH6270

    FAPD-AI: Representative Palmer moved to suspend the rules and pass H.R. 7934, the "Settlement Agreement Information Database Act of 2026," which would add section 307 to subchapter I of chapter 3 of title 5, United States Code. The section requires agencies to establish and maintain public online databases of covered settlement agreements within two years of enactment, with covered agreements including those requiring at least $10,000,000 in explicitly obligated payments, those involving a special master or monitor, and those involving a non-Federal government party, subject to listed exemptions. The bill also directs the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, in coordination with the Attorney General, to issue implementing guidance and requires agencies to submit annual reports on covered agreements not publicly disclosed. CREC-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: Senator Durbin, with cosponsors, introduced S. 5767, the Student Loan Borrower Bill of Rights, which was referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions, and its text was ordered printed in the Record. The bill would amend the Higher Education Act of 1965 to require lender and servicer statements about servicemember and veteran benefits and repayment specialist contacts, to allow prepayment of student loans without penalty with specified rules for applying prepayments, and to require contracted servicers to respond to and share consumer complaints. It would also bar contracted entities from marketing financial products to borrowers using data or contact obtained through the contract and direct a review of legacy servicing contracts within 180 days after enactment. The printed text amends sections 433, 455, and 456 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 to address borrower statements, prepayment and payment allocation, Consumer Financial Protection Act applicability for contracted servicers, complaint handling, and limits on marketing.     FAPD-AI: Mr. Bennet submitted amendment SA 7024 to H.R. 2347, proposing to replace pages 449 through 494 of the bill with new text on tribal programs and related definitions. The text adds Section 302707 to chapter 3027 of title 54, United States Code, which requires the governing body of an Indian tribe to give express written consent before the Secretary may perform functions of a tribal preservation officer, provides for technical assistance and oversight, and sets audit and due-process requirements, including at least two years to cure a covered deficiency, before funds may be withheld. The text also amends section 306108 of title 54 to define terms such as adverse effect of the undertaking, area of potential effects, and undertaking, and the amendment was ordered to lie on the table.     Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES · FR-2026-11-19 / 2026-23429

    official summary: The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS or “Department”) is issuing this final rule to modify the Standards for Privacy of Individually Identifiable Health Information (“Privacy Rule”) under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) and the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health (HITECH) Act. These modifications address standards that may impede the nationwide transition to value-based health care by limiting or discouraging individual access or care coordination and case management or posing other unnecessary burdens. The modifications in this final rule promote the essential sharing of individuals' protected health information (PHI) for care coordination and individual engagement while continuing to protect its privacy and security.     Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE · FR-2026-11-19 / 2026-23529

    official summary: In this interim final rule (IFR), the Department of Commerce is establishing new rules to prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on U.S. technology to threaten U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. First, this rule establishes new restrictions which will apply for exports, reexports, or transfers (in-country) to overseas data centers that remotely supply significant volumes of compute to companies headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau. These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models. Data centers, foreign foundries, and chip exporters are required to perform robust due diligence on their customers, including any direct or indirect ownership or control by persons in Country Group D:5 or Macau, as part of complying with this new control. The license requirement will not apply to commercial recommender systems, such as those used by online retailers or social media companies, as these functions do not pose the same national security threat. [official summary truncated; see source] FR-SEL-01

    official summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2026-12-08, which applies to all Airbus Helicopters Model AS350B2, AS350B3, EC130B4, and EC130T2 helicopters. AD 2026-12-08 requires revising the airworthiness limitations section (ALS) of the existing maintenance manual (MM) or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. Since the FAA issued AD 2026-12-08, a determination was made that new and more restrictive airworthiness limitations and maintenance tasks are necessary. This proposed AD would require incorporating these airworthiness limitations and maintenance tasks into the ALS of the existing MM or ICA and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-02

    Veteran Readiness and Employment Program: Update to Reduced Work Tolerance and Basic Eligibility Period (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS · FR-2026-11-19 / 2026-23571

    official summary: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) proposes to amend the Veteran Readiness and Employment (VR&E) regulations to align with current practice and statute. The rule would expand the list of approved providers for reduced work tolerance (RWT) documentation, allowing for more accurate and timely processing by a Vocational Rehabilitation Counselor (VRC). VA also proposes to clarify that a veteran who is subject to a basic period of eligibility would receive a new 12-year period of eligibility if such veteran obtains a compensable service-connected disability rating based on a subsequent period of active-duty service. Finally, the rule would remove the eligibility termination date for veterans discharged on or after January 1, 2013, consistent with the Johnny Isakson and David P. Roe, M.D. Veterans Health Care and Benefits Improvement Act of 2020. FR-SEL-02

    official summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model EC135P1, EC135P2, EC135P2+, EC135P3, EC135T1, EC135T2, EC135T2+, EC135T3 and EC635T2+ helicopters. This proposed AD was prompted by a determination that the manufacturer's service material does not provide complete instructions for the inspections after a hard landing. This proposed AD would require a one-time inspection of the tail rotor control system and, depending on the inspection results, corrective actions. This proposed AD would also require revision of the existing aircraft maintenance manual (MM) or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-02

    Customer Due Diligence Requirements for Covered Financial Institutions (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF THE TREASURY · FR-2026-11-19 / 2026-23614

    official summary: FinCEN is issuing this proposed rule to strengthen customer due diligence requirements under the Customer Due Diligence Rule consistent with the policy goals of, and as directed by, Executive Order 14406, Restoring Integrity to America's Financial System. Specifically, the proposal ensures financial institutions covered by the Customer Due Diligence Rule collect sufficient information to verify the identities of beneficial owners of legal entity customers and maintain the authority, where warranted, to obtain additional information, including information relevant to whether the beneficial owners of legal entity customers possess lawful immigration status and employment authorization in the United States when such information is relevant to assessing risks. FR-SEL-02

    Airworthiness Directives; General Atomics AeroTec Systems GmbH (Type Certificate Previously Held by RUAG Aerospace Serv… (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION · FR-2026-11-19 / 2026-23633

    official summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all General Atomics AeroTec Systems GmbH (General Atomics) Model Dornier 228-100, Dornier 228-101, Dornier 228-200, Dornier 228-201, Dornier 228-202, and Dornier 228-212 airplanes. This AD was prompted by reports of specific part-numbered hydraulic pump motors becoming severely damaged by excessive heat. This AD requires replacing the affected hydraulic pump motor with an improved design hydraulic pump motor. This AD also prohibits installing an affected hydraulic pump motor on any airplane. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-01
